title: Mitkä: selecting several things
summary: Mitkä selects several identifiable things from a group: Mitkä kirjat ovat uusia? Mitkä kirjat ovat uusia? — Nämä kirjat ovat uusia.
prerequisiteSkills: Mikä: identifying or choosing one thing
objectives: Use mitkä to select several identifiable things.
Identify the selected group without confusing selection with classification.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: Plural means more than one in this grammatical pattern.
A stem is the part of a word to which an ending is attached.
The partitive is a word form used here for an amount, an action's object, or a substance or group description.
Mitkä selects several identifiable things from a group: Mitkä kirjat ovat uusia? (“Which books are new?”). The accompanying noun takes its plural basic form.
keyPoints: Do not use singular mikä to select several things or confuse selection with mitä classification.

sections.title: Answering the question
paragraphs: Identify the selected group with a plural phrase: Nämä kirjat ovat uusia (“These books are new”). The supplied descriptive forms explain the selected items. This is selection, distinct from Mitä nämä ovat? (“What are these?”), which asks for classification.
A natural short reply to “Mitkä kirjat ovat uusia?” is “Nämä kirjat.” (“These books.”). Use the full reply when it makes the person, action or correction clearer.
When a selection is wrong, reject that group and identify the actual group. The whole negative phrase eivät ole is provided; the following description retains its plural form.
The exercises show supporting Finnish words and their meanings when recalling them is not the task. Read the complete English meaning before choosing the question or answer form.
keyPoints: Use a plural identifying phrase for the selected group.

sections.title: Build the answer forms
paragraphs: Nämä means these here. Nämä is the plural basic form of tämä and agrees with the following plural noun.
kirjat means books here. Kirja + plural -t gives kirjat.
Nuo means those here. Nuo is the plural basic form of tuo and agrees with the following plural noun.
autot means cars here. Auto + plural -t gives autot.
kynät means pens here. Kynä + plural -t gives kynät.
laukut means bags here. Laukku changes kk to k before plural -t: laukut.
puhelimet means phones here. Puhelin uses the stem puhelime- and plural -t: puhelimet.
avaimet means keys here. Avain uses the stem avaime- before plural -t: avaimet.
pallot means balls here. Pallo + plural -t gives pallot.
keyPoints: Use a plural identifying phrase for the selected group.

ole: be; main verb after the negative verb. After a present-tense negative verb, olla takes the unchanged form ole.
